title: Lemony Miso Cabbage
ingredients: 1 lb green cabbage, chopped into 1-inch pieces, layers separated (about 6 cups)
steps: Whisk the miso with 1/4 cup water in a small bowl, mashing until it fully dissolves.
Melt the butter in a 12-inch nonstick skillet (one with a lid) over medium-high. Add the cabbage, season with salt and pepper, and stir to coat in the butter, about 1 min.
Drizzle the miso mixture over the top and stir it through. Cover and cook until the cabbage is just softened, about 2 min.

Uncover, mix well, then spread the cabbage into an even layer. Leave it undisturbed until the liquid has cooked off and the underside is lightly golden, about 2 min - this is where the sweetness comes from.
Turn off the heat. Add the lemon juice and dill and mix, scraping up any browned bits. Taste and season again with salt and pepper.
Transfer to a shallow bowl. Good warm or at room temperature.
notes: Butter + miso makes a silky savory sauce that carries the cabbage; the lemon and dill at the end cut the richness. Steam first, then caramelize - do not stir during the browning step or it just steams. Side dish for pan-roasted chicken, fish or steak, and good over rice or noodles. Five ingredients, one pan, about 15 minutes.

title: Quick Chicken Laksa
ingredients: 3-4 Tbsp shop-bought laksa paste (or red curry paste)
1/4 cucumber, cut into very thin matchsticks
steps: Boil a large saucepan of water. Cook the eggs 6 min, then drop them into cold water and leave until needed.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium-high. Fry the laksa paste 2-3 min, until the oil turns reddish - that colour change is the cue it has bloomed.
Stir in the chicken stock, coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar. Cover and bring to the boil.
Add the chicken breast, re-cover, drop to medium and cook 10-12 min, until cooked through.
Meanwhile put the vermicelli in a large heatproof bowl, pour over 1 litre of just-boiled water to cover, and leave to soak while the chicken cooks. Drain just before serving.
Lift the chicken out to a plate and keep the soup warm over low heat. Let the chicken cool enough to handle, then shred it into chunks with forks or your hands.
Divide the drained noodles between two bowls, top with the shredded chicken, and ladle over enough soup to just cover the noodles.
Peel and halve the eggs and add to the bowls. Garnish with cucumber, mint, coriander and chilli; serve with lime wedges.
notes: From the BBC Food reel (@bbcfood) - Justin Tsang's shortcut on a dish that traditionally takes hours. The shop-bought paste is doing the heavy lifting, so the brand matters: laksa paste is the real thing, red curry paste is the fallback. 6-minute eggs give a jammy yolk; add a minute if you want them firmer. Pour the soup over the noodles only to cover - drowning them makes it watery. About 900 kcal per serving as written; use light coconut milk to cut it back.

title: Thai Green Curry Lentil Soup
ingredients: 1 (4-oz) package sliced mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, shiitake)
1 (1-inch) piece fresh ginger, peeled and finely chopped (about 2 Tbsp)
2 large garlic cloves, finely chopped (about 1 Tbsp)
1 bunch scallions, dark greens separated from white and light green, thinly sliced
1/4 cup green curry paste (Maesri or similar)
2 cups peeled butternut squash, 1/2-inch chop (about 12 oz)
1 bunch fresh cilantro with tender stems, coarsely chopped, plus more to garnish
1 tsp fish sauce (Red Boat or similar)
Thinly sliced Fresno chile, to garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a medium Dutch oven over medium-high until shimmering. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone until browned on one side, 3-4 min. Stir and keep cooking until tender, about 2 min more.

Add the ginger, garlic, and the white and light green scallion, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 min. Stir in the curry paste and cook, stirring, 1 min more - blooming it in the oil is what deepens the broth.
Add the broth and squash. Bring to a boil, then drop to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the squash is tender, 10-12 min.
While it simmers: set aside 1/4 cup of the coconut milk for drizzling. Put the rest in a blender with the cilantro, miso and scallion greens. Blend smooth, about 30 seconds.

Stir the lentils into the pot, breaking up any clumps. Add the fish sauce, salt, and the blended coconut mixture. Cook over medium, stirring often, just until warmed through, about 2 min - no longer, or the green fades.
Ladle into bowls, drizzle with the reserved coconut milk, and top with Fresno chile and more cilantro. Lime wedges at the table.
notes: Lentil swaps: cooked French green lentils are closest - they hold their shape like black lentils. Brown or green work but go softer. Skip red lentils, they dissolve. Frozen butternut is fine straight from frozen; it softens faster and releases water, so start checking early. Mushrooms: spread them out and do not stir for the first few minutes or they steam instead of browning. Green curry pastes vary a lot in heat and salt - taste before the final seasoning. Vegetarian: use vegetable broth and skip the fish sauce (add a little extra miso or salt). Serve as-is, or over steamed jasmine rice for a bigger dinner.
